Crypto lender Nimbus accused by US regulator of misleading 90,000 savers

Published 2026-10-06 17:30 UTC

The US financial regulator has accused the crypto lender Nimbus Lending of misleading more than 90,000 savers in a $1.2bn scheme, in the latest crackdown on the crypto industry.

The Securities and Exchange Commission said Nimbus and its founder, Mark Ellery, promised returns of up to 14% a year through a product called Yield Vault, claiming the money was lent to institutional borrowers. Instead, the SEC alleges, deposits from new customers were used to pay existing ones, and Ellery diverted more than $40m.

Nimbus froze customer withdrawals in August. Ellery's lawyers said he denied wrongdoing. Consumer groups said the case showed the need for tougher rules on crypto lending platforms.

The SEC alleges that Nimbus told savers their money was safe and that loans were fully collateralised, while it was secretly funnelling hundreds of millions of dollars to a trading firm controlled by its founder, Mark Ellery. Many of the 90,000 savers were retail customers who had moved savings into the app in search of higher returns.

Nimbus froze withdrawals last year when crypto prices fell sharply and the trading firm suffered heavy losses. The company later filed for bankruptcy. Customers have recovered only a fraction of their deposits so far, and some have described losing life savings in online forums.

Consumer advocates said the case highlights the risks of products that look like savings accounts but lack deposit insurance and the protections offered by regulated banks. They called for clearer warnings on crypto apps and stricter rules for how such platforms advertise.

Ellery's lawyers said he will contest the charges. The SEC is seeking penalties and the return of profits, and any recovered money may be distributed to harmed customers. In the UK, the Financial Conduct Authority has warned consumers that crypto lending products are high risk and not covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.
